guide.title: Aurora AR-900 Configuration and Troubleshooting Guide

sections.heading: BGP configuration and next-hop resolution
key_facts: On 9.1.4 and 9.1.6, clear the BGP process for the affected IPv4 unicast address family if the next-hop remains unresolved after an underlay route withdrawal.
If the affected path is critical during a maintenance window, prefer a static discard route with a lower administrative distance than the learned underlay route so recursion remains stable.

On 9.2.3, issue a soft clear of the affected BGP address family after changing recursive static routes, and if a clear must be avoided, withdraw the old static route for at least 5 seconds before installing the replacement.
Avoid repeated soft clears during peak update periods, because the routing process can spike to 95% CPU on 9.2.1.

sections.heading: BFD timer tuning and long-uptime maintenance
key_facts: On 9.1.4, restart the BFD process or reload the router during a maintenance window before platform uptime reaches 49 days.
As temporary containment on noncritical peers, set the BFD transmit interval to 200 ms and the detection multiplier to 5.
Use the same 200/200/5 timer profile consistently on peers where transient loss is acceptable, and verify the session state after the change.
If BFD stops transmitting after long uptime, treat it as a process recovery issue rather than a link-layer fault and plan a controlled restart.

sections.heading: OSPF adjacency stability on multiaccess segments
key_facts: On 9.2.0, match the MTU on both sides of a multiaccess segment to prevent repeated OSPF adjacency resets.
If the topology permits, configure the neighbor or interface as point-to-point instead of multiaccess to avoid MTU negotiation instability.
When MTU cannot be matched during the maintenance window, enable `ip ospf mtu-ignore` on both peers.
After applying the workaround, confirm the adjacency reaches full state and does not restart on the next hello dead interval.

sections.heading: IPv6 neighbor discovery and router advertisement handling
key_facts: Do not suppress router advertisements on the active user VLAN when SLAAC is in use, because prefixes can be removed too early after suppression.
If RA suppression is required, use DHCPv6 stateful addressing on the affected segment rather than relying on SLAAC.
Keep the RA hold timer above the preferred lifetime so hosts do not age out prefixes prematurely.
Review the VLAN interface configuration before changing suppression behavior to ensure the access segment keeps a valid IPv6 addressing method.

sections.heading: QoS and control-plane protection thresholds
key_facts: On 9.2.1, cap the strict-priority class at 30% bandwidth to prevent best-effort starvation during microbursts.
Where strict priority is not required, convert the service class to low-latency queueing with an explicit policer of 300 Mbps on 10 Gbps links.
On 9.2.3, set the control-plane policer for IPv6 ND to 2,000 pps until the traffic source is identified.
Reduce IPv6 ND load at the edge with RA guard or storm control on the access VLAN, and if necessary shut the offending access port for 30 seconds to let neighbor state recover.

sections.heading: SNMP trap reliability and NAT capacity management
key_facts: If trap history must be complete, shorten the SNMP polling interval to 30 seconds and treat traps as advisory when link flap storms are present.
Enable link debounce of 500 ms on unstable access ports to reduce linkUp trap loss when the trap queue exceeds 1024 entries.
On 9.3.0, increase the NAT pool size or add at least one additional public address if dynamic NAT port exhaustion is reported incorrectly after teardown.
If session churn is predictable, increase application keepalive intervals to 60 seconds or more and set the NAT translation timeout to 240 seconds to reduce allocator churn.

guide.title: nimbus nf-300 configuration and troubleshooting guide

sections.heading: ipsec and ikev2 tunnel setup
key_facts: For policy-based IKEv2 tunnels, avoid local selectors narrower than /30; use route-based VPN for host-to-host designs and enforce restrictions with firewall policy instead.
On 5.1.3 and 5.1.5, pin a single DH group on both peers, preferably group 14, and avoid mixed transform sets to prevent phase 2 resets.
On 5.0.8 and 5.0.9, keep the PFS group unchanged on both peers; if a change is required, apply the same group on both sides and clear the SA after the change.
If the platform is rekeying active traffic and a child SA change is required on 5.0.8 or 5.0.9, disable child SA rekey and schedule a manual tunnel restart during a maintenance window.

sections.heading: ha pair stability and resynchronization
key_facts: Place HA heartbeat links on a dedicated L2 segment that is independent of monitored interfaces to prevent oscillation.
If dedicated cabling is not immediately possible, set the HA monitor interval to 10 seconds so transient link events are less likely to trigger repeated failover.
On 5.0.9 after split-brain recovery, perform a full HA resync instead of relying on incremental replay.
After node return, keep failover links stable for at least 120 seconds so the replay queue can drain before you validate session state.

sections.heading: session-table tuning for asymmetric traffic
key_facts: On 5.2.0, if asymmetric routing is enabled for large-prefix traffic, disable it for the affected policy set when shard imbalance appears.
For concentrated /24 traffic, split the prefix into smaller policy groups so sessions distribute more evenly across shards.
Keep the busiest shard below 75 percent occupancy until a software fix is available, and verify distribution after each policy change.
Use session-table summary output to confirm that the hottest shard is not trending upward across successive samples.

sections.heading: ssl inspection cache and policy change handling
key_facts: On 5.2.0 and 5.2.2, increase the SSL inspection certificate cache size to 4096 entries to reduce eviction-driven bypass events.
If outbound TLS inspection starts bypassing intermittently after cache eviction, restart SSL inspection to clear stale pointers as a temporary recovery step.
Disable outbound inspection for the affected server group only if the cache increase does not keep evictions below 1,000 entries per hour.
Avoid changing SSL inspection policy while a threat database update is active, because activation can stall packet processing on 5.1.5.

sections.heading: firmware upgrade preparation and image staging
key_facts: Before upgrading from 5.0.x to 5.1.3 or 5.1.5, keep each checkpoint file under 4,000 entries and verify the running configuration immediately after reboot.
If the configuration contains more than 4,096 replay entries, split the upgrade into smaller chunks or export and re-import policy objects after first boot.
On 5.0.8, stage 5.0.9 images with SCP or USB rather than HTTPS so the boot loader does not reject a valid image because of padding.
Always verify the staged image hash before scheduling the reboot and confirm the image appears in software inventory.

sections.heading: threat database updates and timing control
key_facts: On 5.1.5, schedule threat database updates during a maintenance window and keep the signature bundle below 128 MB to avoid packet-processing stalls.
Set the update window to 02:00 through 02:15 when operationally feasible, and avoid SSL inspection policy changes until activation completes.
Use the threat database status output to confirm whether an update is active before making any inspection or policy changes.
If a large bundle is unavoidable, defer nonessential traffic-policy edits until the update has fully applied and the dataplane has returned to steady state.

guide.title: Orion OW-20 Configuration and Troubleshooting Guide

sections.heading: AP join baseline and retry tuning
key_facts: For AP join failures on 4.6, remove any RF profile override from the AP group so the controller does not emit a zero-length RF profile TLV.
On 4.7, set the AP join retry interval to 2 seconds so the controller keeps the transaction active through capability revalidation.
On 4.8, set the AP join timeout to 180 seconds when join stalls occur during the second capability exchange.
For remote APs, keep one-way latency under 80 ms on 4.7 systems and keep uplink loss below 0.5% during 4.8 join operations.

sections.heading: Controller redundancy and configuration database hygiene
key_facts: Keep the configuration database below 30,000 rows before enabling redundancy to avoid sync stalls at the 32,768-row threshold.
Remove unused AP groups, WLAN profiles, and stale guest accounts before enabling active-standby operation.
If immediate failover is required after a large configuration change, schedule a full config resync during a maintenance window.
Use redundancy force-resync only after confirming the database has been reduced and the commit queue is clear.

sections.heading: 802.11r roaming validation and load control
key_facts: For 4.9, keep controller CPU below 70% during roaming tests to reduce fast-transition key installation delays.
Lower the client accounting interval to 60 seconds on latency-sensitive SSIDs when 802.11r is enabled.
For 5.0, stagger roaming tests or reduce the client cleanup batch size so the FT flush completes within 150 ms.
Cap roam bursts below 30 clients per 10 seconds on voice-critical SSIDs until the affected release is updated.

sections.heading: RADIUS Access-Challenge attribute ordering
key_facts: On 4.9, keep Access-Challenge replies at 12 or fewer attributes to avoid loss or omission of Vendor-Specific attribute 26.
If the server must send more than 12 attributes, move Vendor-Specific attribute 26 earlier in the response order.
Prefer a policy server that sends tunneled attributes first when troubleshooting intermittent 802.1X challenge processing.
Use the vendor-first attribute order setting before retesting client authentication.

sections.heading: Guest portal sessions across failover
key_facts: During guest registration windows, keep failover inhibited so portal cookies remain pinned to the active node UUID.
For planned maintenance, set guest portal session timeout to 15 minutes before invoking failover.
If a switchover already occurred, clear the portal cookie and require the guest to reauthenticate.
Expire guest sessions before a planned redundancy failover when guest access continuity matters.

sections.heading: 5.1 RF manager and upgrade readiness
key_facts: On 5.1, disable DFS on affected radio groups if repeated DFS events stop channel updates.
Pin radios to a non-DFS channel set such as 36,40,44,48 with at least 20 MHz separation from neighboring cells.
Keep radar events below 3 per 10 minutes during peak usage if DFS must remain enabled.
Before upgrading from 4.6 to 5.0, delete unused legacy guest portal ACL objects and verify the configuration database contains only normalized entries.

guide.title: Atlas SD-WAN Configuration and Troubleshooting Guide

sections.heading: SLA class stability and probe tuning
key_facts: Use a probe window of at least five samples so a single 1-second loss spike does not clear the SLA class.
Set the hold-down to 5000 ms before allowing the class to recover, which prevents rapid down/up transitions on marginal links.
For links that are already close to threshold, raise the packet-loss threshold by 1 to 2 percent to avoid unnecessary path switching.
Keep the probe interval at 1000 ms for voice or other latency-sensitive classes unless a site-specific design requires a slower cadence.
commands: app-route sla-class voice loss-threshold 5 latency-threshold 80 probe-interval 1000 hold-down 5000

sections.heading: Certificate chain maintenance and edge re-registration
key_facts: Reimport the full certificate chain, including the active intermediate CA, on the orchestrator before renewing any edge certificate.
Stage the new chain at least 24 hours before the old intermediate expires so renewal and re-registration do not fail during the cutover window.
If edge re-registration fails after renewal, verify that the orchestrator trust bundle contains the current intermediate and root chain in the same import set.

sections.heading: Policy push limits, CRL freshness, and route-map sizing
key_facts: Keep each route-map at 256 entries or fewer; split larger maps into separate policy objects before the push.
If a tenant already has a larger route-map, remove 10 to 20 entries, commit the change, and re-add the remainder in a second commit to unblock policy push.
Refresh the CRL before it is older than 24 hours, or align CA publication to a 12 to 18 hour interval so the push window does not hit the hard-expiry check.
Confirm the updated CRL timestamp before retrying a failed policy push.

sections.heading: LTE tunnel MTU and handoff tuning
key_facts: After any 3.1 upgrade, reapply the LTE tunnel MTU on each dual-SIM edge because the upgrade may rewrite it to 1500.
For most carrier LTE links, use a tunnel MTU between 1400 and 1420 bytes; validate the path with 1472-byte pings before returning the site to service.
On 3.2 systems with custom APN profiles, recheck every LTE interface after migration because the per-interface tunnel MTU can be dropped.
For 3.3 edges with both modems enabled, set the LTE handoff debounce to 5000 ms to reduce CPU spikes during transient signal loss.

sections.heading: Overlay tunnel queueing and routing-cache hygiene
key_facts: Place SLA probes into a high-priority queue on busy links so burst traffic does not delay probe packets and flap the overlay tunnel.
If shaping is already enabled, reduce the bulk-traffic class to 60 to 70 percent so control traffic is not queued behind large data bursts.
After a planned underlay withdrawal, trigger a route-refresh or shorten the app-route cache age-time to 60 seconds during the maintenance window.
Confirm that withdrawn routes disappear from the cache before moving traffic to the backup link.

sections.heading: Reporting load control and operational verification
key_facts: Reduce flow-history retention to 5 days when reporting jobs are consuming excessive CPU on 3.3 systems.
If the environment requires longer retention, split reports into narrower 24-hour jobs and schedule them during a low-change maintenance window.
Use reporting window changes to avoid contention with policy updates on the same CPU cores.
Verify tunnel state and application-route status after report tuning so operational troubleshooting is not confused by delayed analytics processing.

guide.title: Helix HX-5000 Configuration and Troubleshooting Guide

sections.heading: Optics and transceiver health checks
key_facts: On 7.2, reduce DOM polling on affected SFP28 ports by setting the transceiver monitoring interval to 120 seconds.
Keep optics below 50 C case temperature when possible, especially on ports showing bias current spikes or remote LOS alarms.
If a port continues to flap under load, move the optic to a later-release port or replace the module with one that has a stable bias current profile.

sections.heading: Stack stability and master election
key_facts: On 7.3, use matched-length stack cables between all members to reduce master election oscillation.
Keep control-plane load below 60 percent until the software is upgraded, because higher load increases the chance of unstable master changes.
Pin the desired master by setting a higher priority value on the preferred member and avoid adding or removing members during the unstable period.
On 7.6, keep stack cabling under 1 m when possible and avoid chaining all members through a single long physical path.

sections.heading: Spanning tree behavior on access ports
key_facts: Do not run rapid-pvst on ports facing devices that legitimately move multiple MAC addresses, such as virtualization hosts or clustered appliances.
Use a dedicated edge VLAN design or restrict the port to a single access device when rapid-pvst is required.
Apply portfast on edge ports to reduce convergence delay, but only on interfaces that do not participate in downstream bridging.
Monitor for continuous topology-change notifications on 10G access ports and reclassify the port role if the notifications persist.

sections.heading: LACP and EtherChannel member handling
key_facts: On 7.4, configure both ends of the bundle for fast LACP timers if the design permits it.
If the peer advertises slow timers and the bundle mis-bundles or suspends members, switch the local port-channel to fast LACP timers.
When the bundle must remain on slow timers, do not flap individual member links during maintenance and clear the EtherChannel only after link restoration.

sections.heading: EVPN route handling and memory protection
key_facts: On 7.6, trigger a controlled EVPN route refresh after moving the anycast gateway MAC.
Avoid gateway MAC mobility during periods when the fabric is carrying active type-5 routes, and keep the gateway anchored on a single leaf pair when possible.
On 7.6, reduce unnecessary neighbor resets and schedule a reload before free memory drops below 15 percent.
If route-refresh events are unavoidable, keep EVPN adjacency changes out of peak traffic windows.

sections.heading: Queue, buffer, and burst management
key_facts: On 7.2, reduce burstiness with upstream shaping or spread load across additional uplinks so no single egress port stays above 85 percent sustained utilization.
For critical low-latency flows on oversubscribed 100G egress ports, reserve a dedicated queue on the affected interface.
On 8.0, limit multicast fanout on busy leafs or move replication-heavy workloads onto a separate uplink group to protect the shared buffer pool.
If multicast bursts are predictable, schedule the traffic outside congestion-sensitive windows and tune the multicast reservation to 12 percent with a 4096 cell queue limit where required.
